content.text: This document specifies the binary X-message format that MRV ALAMO and ALTO profiling floats use to send their data over Iridium Short Burst Data (SBD). It also says how XMTPS decodes each message and which listing-file lines each message becomes.
Status: compiled on 2026-10-25. It brings together everything known about the format:

items.text: the SOLO-II X-format specification it derives from;
the ALAMO X-format spreadsheet (v2.4);
MRV's firmware message definitions (7.3.5, 10.5.0, 10.12.0);
the XMTPS decoder source;
hand-decoded production packets.

**Structure.** A float's data for one dive cycle is split into *packets*. Each packet travels as one Iridium SBD message, a binary e-mail attachment of at most 340 bytes. A packet has the form `X nn mm dd p <data> $cc>`, and its `<data>` is a sequence of *blobs* (the SOLO-II documents call them "sensor messages"). Each blob has the form `ID jj <data> ;`. The 1-byte ID says what the blob holds; `jj` is the blob length. Part A.1 gives the details.
**Offsets** in every table count from the blob's ID byte, which is offset 0. All multi-byte fields are big-endian, including the IEEE-754 floats.
**Times** are seconds since 2000-01-01 00:00 UTC unless a table says UNIX time (seconds since 1970-01-01).
**Sensor values** sent as counts are converted with the gains and offsets in the same dive's Argo message 0xF0: `value = counts / gain − offset` (A.1.5).

`u8/u16/u24/u32` are unsigned and `i8/i16/i24/i32` are two's-complement signed big-endian integers. `u4` / `u20` denote nibble-aligned fields that share a byte with a neighbor (see the Notes column).

sections.heading: A.1.1 Transport: Iridium SBD and the mail gateway
sections.title: Transport: Iridium SBD and the mail gateway

items.text: The float stores telemetry in an on-board "XMessage file system" (XFS) of 1500 blocks [M `xfs.txt`]. **One XFS block = one Iridium SBD mobile-originated message = one X packet.**

An SBD message carries at most **340 bytes**. The X packet header (8 bytes: `X nn mm dd p`) and trailer (4 bytes: `$cc>`) take 12, so a block carries at most **328 bytes of blobs** [M]. (SOLO-II documentation still refers to the 189-byte 9601 limit [S]; it doesn't apply to ALAMO/ALTO.)

A block holds one or more complete blobs, end to end with no gaps. All blobs in a block belong to the same dive. **A blob never spans two packets.** Multi-part data (profiles, time series) is split into separate blobs that carry their own part index [M][D].
The Iridium gateway forwards each SBD message as an e-mail [D `XFloatMailMessage.h`]:
Sender matches `(sbdservice@sbd.iridium.com|service@sbd.pac.disa.mil)`. This is configurable.
Subject matches `SBD Msg From Unit: (\d+)`, which gives the IMEI.
The binary attachment (MIME type `application/*`) is named `<IMEI>_<MOMSN, 6 digits>.sbd` (regex `(\d+)_(\d{6})\.sbd`). Its bytes are the X packet.
The body text gives `MOMSN:`, `MTMSN:`, `Time of Session (UTC):`, `Session Status: NN - text`, `Message Size (bytes):`, `Unit Location: Lat = … Long = …` and `CEPradius = N` (km).

The decoder accepts the attachment only if it has at least **8 bytes** (`XMSG_SBD_MIN_BYTES`) and the session status is **00 or 02** (transfer OK; 02 = OK but the location is of unacceptable quality) [D].
Duplicates [D]:
A mail with an already-seen Message-ID is ignored.
A mail whose SBD bytes are identical to an already-assigned packet of the dive is a retransmission under a new MOMSN. It is kept for its Iridium position, but its blobs are not decoded again.
Dive data is keyed by (serial number, dive number) taken from the packet header, not from the e-mail.
Transmission order is not packet-ID order. In the observed dives the highest `p` was sent first and `p = 0` last [O].

sections.heading: A.1.2 X packet: `X nn mm dd p <data> $ c c >`

rows: Start marker. Not checked by the decoder [D].
Number of bytes after `nn` up to, but not including, `$` = 5 + len(`<data>`) [S]. Verified: `nn` = packet length − 7 on 27 packets [O]. Ignored by the decoder, which uses the attachment length [D].
Dive (cycle) number: −1 = start-up, 0 = test/diagnostic dive, then +1 per dive [S]. Signed [D].
Packet ID within the dive. The data of each dive starts at `p = 0` [S]. Listed as `PID` on `SBD` lines.

content.text: **Checksum.** `sum = (Σ bytes from 'X' (offset 0) through the byte before '$') mod 256`. It is written as two characters, high nibble first, each nibble + 0x30. So the characters are in the range `0`–`?` (`0x3A`–`0x3F` = `:;<=>?` stand for nibble values 10–15) [S]. All 1,351,052 X packets in the production RAW files (all floats and firmware, 2014–2026) have a correct checksum [O].

**Decoder note [D]:** since build 3310 the decoder verifies the checksum (`XFloatDiveData::DecodeXMsgData`). A packet whose checksum does not match is discarded and logged ("X-Message checksum mismatch"); a packet without the `$cc>` trailer is decoded with a warning. The blob parser reads offsets 8 … len−5.

rows: High nibble = message class; low nibble = part index or sub-type (e.g. 0x1n = binned pressure, part n). For classes with a single type (0xD0, 0xDE, 0xE0–0xEC, 0xF0, 0xF1) the whole byte is the type.
Blob length in bytes, **including** ID, `jj` and the trailing `;`. Two layouts, see below.

content.text: **`jj` layouts:**

items.text: **Encoding nibble + 12-bit size**, used by the sensor/time-series families: 0x1n–0x3n, 0x4n, 0x5n, 0x6n, 0x78–0x7F, 0x8n, 0x9n, 0xAn, 0xBn and 0xDC. Bits 15–12 of `jj` (high nibble of byte 1) hold the packing/encoding format; bits 11–0 hold the size (0–4095) [S][X].
**Full 16-bit size**, used by GPS 0x00–0x05, 0xC1, 0xD0–0xD7, 0xDE, 0xE5–0xEC (including the valve message 0xEB) and 0xF0 [X]. Here the encoding format, if any, is in byte 3 (e.g. 0xEB).
Exception: SOLO-legacy pump format 0 (0x6n with format nibble 0) is read with the full 16-bit size by `XPump` [D], which is equivalent because the high nibble is then 0.

content.text: **How the decoder splits a packet into blobs [D] (`XFloatDiveData::DecodeXMsgData`):**

items.text: Bytes 8 … len−5 are appended one at a time to a buffer.

At 3 buffered bytes the size is taken as `0x0FFF & u16(buf, 1)`. **The 12-bit mask is applied to every type.** This is harmless because a blob is always smaller than 4096 bytes (SBD ≤ 340), so the high nibble of a 16-bit size is always 0.
When the buffer reaches the size, the blob is dispatched on its ID byte and the buffer is cleared. A trailing incomplete blob is silently dropped. A wrong size desynchronizes the rest of the packet.

Each class decoder checks the ID, a minimum length, and that `buf[size−1] == ';'` (most of them via `XMessage::CheckXMsgData`; the size must be at least 4). Extra bytes produce a warning; a missing terminator is an error.
IDs without a decoder are logged as `Unknown X message ID: 0x..` and skipped, for example 0xC2 and 0x70–0x77 (and 0xFF before build 3321, C.6). 0xF1 (test pattern) is ignored silently.

sections.heading: A.1.4 Byte order, bit order, epochs
sections.title: Byte order, bit order, epochs

items.text: **Big-endian** everywhere: multi-byte integers are sent MSB first [S][D].

Bit fields are numbered from the MSB of the first byte. In a byte that holds two nibbles, the **high nibble comes first**. For example, a "code + 20-bit pressure" field is `code = b[k] >> 4`, `pres = ((b[k] & 0x0F) << 16) | b[k+1] << 8 | b[k+2]`.
**Time epochs:**

**2000-01-01T00:00:00Z** (`s2000`): u32 seconds since this epoch for the 0xF0 state start times and the fall/rise/surface start/reference times. **0 means "not set"**: the decoder maps it to not-a-date-time, listed as `0000-00-00T00:00:00Z` [D]. The spreadsheet's "offset 36526" on these fields is the Excel day number of 2000-01-01 [X].
**GPS epoch 1980-01-06**: GPS week and day in the GPS message (A.2).
**UNIX epoch 1970-01-01** (`s1970`): used only by the BIT v2 engineering message (`XAlamoBit2.h`, outside this part) [D].
Relative times: u16 seconds after a reference (fall/rise/surface), and u24/i24 seconds after the drift start (0x78).
Leap seconds are not applied anywhere [D].

content.text: All CTD quantities (pressure, temperature, salinity) are sent as integer counts:
value = counts / gain − offset

`gain` and `offset` are unsigned 16-bit integers from the 0xF0 Argo message of the **same dive** [D][X][M]. The SOLO-II document gives `counts · gain − offset` in one place [S]; that is a typo, and both its own 0xF0 table and the decoder use division.

rows: Binned/hi-res/drift profiles, 0xDC, aux temperature, fall, rise, pump, valve
surface gains/offsets (0xF0 bytes 52–63). In v2.1 these are copies of the profile gains.

content.text: Typical values [O]:

items.text: **No 0xF0 in the dive** [D]: all gains and offsets are set to 9999 (`IRI_GAIN_INVALID` / `IRI_OFFS_INVALID`), so every converted value falls out of range and is listed as the fill value. The float-level fallback is commented out. A dive's data can only be converted once its own 0xF0 has arrived.
**gain = 0** gives the fill value (the per-message `SampleValue` returns −100 internally).
**Signedness [D]:** composite accessors pass gain/offset as `int16_t`, so a gain above 32767 would be misread. No observed float uses one.
**Valid ranges [D]:** values outside these limits are replaced by the fill value (`XDefinitions.h`):

**Pressure offset correction [D]:** for RBR floats (or WMO instrument types 866/867/875) XMTPS can subtract a surface-pressure offset `pc`, derived from the surface time series of recent dives, from profile, drift, fall, rise, pump and valve pressures. Surface (`sfc`) pressures are always listed uncorrected. See README "Surface pressure offset correction".

Start of dive: just before leaving the surface.

rows: 0 = no/invalid fix; +2 = longitude East; −2 (0xFE) = West [S][X]. The decoder only tests for 0; the sign is also carried by the i32 longitude.
Full week number since 1980-01-06: "traditional" 10-bit week in the low 10 bits, rollover count in the high 6 bits [S], so the u16 is the continuous week number.
Seconds are not sent; the decoder uses 0.
The decoder keeps only the low nibble (`& 0x0F`).

content.text: **Decoding notes [D]:**

items.text: Time = 1980-01-06T00:00 + (week·7 + day) days + hour:minute (UTC).
A fix is set invalid when:
byte 3 = 0;
the coordinates are outside ±90/±180;
the time is before 2000-01-01 or in the future;
(when the fix is assigned) the time is later than the dive's last Iridium session time.
An invalid fix gets lat 99.99999, lon 999.99999 and no time.
A valid 0x05 fix advances the float's start-of-mission time. Packets sent before the start-of-mission or deployment time are ignored.
**Profile position selection:**
A 0x02 fix of the same dive is the profile position.
A 0x01 fix labeled with dive N+1 is valid for dive N.
A 0x00 fix is used only for dive 0.
0x03 and 0x05 are never used as profile positions.
**Listing:** one `GPS` line per fix: `GPS SN dive idx date/time position TTF nSat SNRmin SNRavg SNRmax HDOP stat`. `idx` is the ID (phase) and `stat` is always 0.

content.text: Evidence: this is `AbstractXSensorData::UnpackSensorData` [D]. The documents disagree with it:

items.text: **[S]** says "packing factor 0 = 1 nibble", i.e. width = p+1 nibbles.

**[X]** says width = `pN·4+4` bits (p+1 nibbles) in one sentence, then lists "p=0 → 0 nibble null, p=1 → 1 nibble, …". Its byte counts per sub-block (16, 24, …, 64 bytes for p = 1 … 7) are 8 bytes too large.

content.text: All 24 curvature blobs in the two production dives were checked [O]. Under the decoder rule (p nibbles, p = 0 skipped) the nibble count equals the data length exactly, with at most one pad nibble. Under the p+1 rule every blob would need 30–80 % more bytes than it has. Even all-zero second differences (constant 1800 s steps in 0x78) are sent with p = 1, never p = 0, so p = 0 is used only for unused trailing sub-blocks.
**Unpacking, exactly as the decoder does it [D]:**

items.text: Read B (ignored), NN, VVV (i24) and DDD (i24).
If NN = 0, throw. If NN = 1, the part's values are just [VVV]. If NN = 2, they are [VVV, VVV + DDD]. VVV is included only in the first part; see reassembly. In both cases return.
Otherwise, require size ≥ 24 and read the 32 packing factors.
Set `remaining = NN − 2` and k = 0, and set the nibble cursor to the high nibble of byte 24.
While `remaining > 0` and the cursor is before the terminator:
If k ≥ 32, error.
If p_k = 0, set k += 1 and continue (no data consumed).

Otherwise read n = min(16, remaining) values. For each value read p_k nibbles, most significant first, as an unsigned integer u, then sign-extend: `if u ≥ 2^(4p−1) then u −= 2^(4p)`. Append it to the second differences and decrement `remaining`.
Set k += 1.

**The nibble cursor is continuous across sub-blocks**: sub-blocks are not byte-aligned. Because a full sub-block has 16·p nibbles (always even), only the last sub-block can end mid-byte. The low nibble of the last data byte is then padding.
First differences: `d[0] = DDD`, `d[i] = d[i−1] + s[i−1]`, i = 1 … NN−2 (cumulative sum of the second differences, seeded with DDD).
Values: `x = VVV` (not appended unless this is the first part), then for each first difference `x += d[i]` and append x. That is NN − 1 values, plus VVV for the first part.
If the stream ends before `remaining` reaches 0, the decoder logs a warning and keeps the partial part (it does not throw).

content.text: **Multi-part reassembly [D] (`AbstractXSensorDataComposite`):**

items.text: **The first part includes VVV; later parts don't.** The "first part" is the one whose ID is 0x10, 0x20, 0x30, 0x90, 0xA0, 0xB0, 0x98, 0xA8, 0xB8 or 0x78. Part m > 0 repeats the last value of part m−1 as its VVV (an overlap of one value), and the decoder drops it, so part m contributes NN − 1 values. Total samples = NN₀ + Σ_{m>0} (NN_m − 1).
Verified [O], float 11186 dive 107, temperature 0x20/0x21/0x22 with NN = 306/290/192: 306 + 289 + 191 = 786 samples, the same count as pressure and the aux-temperature channel.

Parts are kept per channel, sorted by part index (the low nibble of the ID), and concatenated in index order. A duplicate index is rejected. The decoder doesn't check that the overlap VVV equals the previous part's last value.

**B** in the observed data is the number of 16-value sub-blocks in all preceding parts of the same channel: 0 for the first part, then 15, 19, 32, 37 … [O]. The SOLO-II document says B = 1 in the first part [S]. Not used by the decoder.
At most 32 sub-blocks per part, so NN ≤ 514 per blob. Observed maximum: 514 [O].
**Completeness** (`IsDataComplete`), required before any `pro`/`pru`/`d` rows are listed:
at least one sample;
part indices contiguous **from the lowest received index** (a missing first part isn't detected by this test alone);
the same number of P and T samples;
aux-temperature samples (if any) equal T;
S samples are 0 or equal P.
Otherwise the listing prints `# (Incomplete … Data)`.
**Missing bins:** a bin with no valid CTD data is simply not sent, so all channels skip the same bin and stay aligned [S]. The decoder has no bin numbers; `sampleIdx` is the position in the series.

items.text: `v[k] = v[k−1] + δk·S`. Sub-blocks hold up to 25 values (1 + 24 differences, 27 bytes); only the last sub-block may be shorter.
Sub-blocks are read back to back until the terminator. Parts concatenate by index **without any overlap**.

sections.title: Drift sample times — 0x78–0x7F  *(format inferred [I]; decoder [D] `XDriftTime.h`)*

content.text: **Purpose.** The time of each drift sample (0x98/0xA8/0xB8 series), in seconds after the Argo `park start time` (0xF0 bytes 20–23). Not in any MRV or spreadsheet document. The format was inferred from production packets (2026-10-24).

items.text: **Layout:** identical to the curvature encoding of A.3.1. ID = 0x78 + part index (0x78 = first part, which includes VVV); format nibble 1.
**Values:** u24 seconds, no gain or offset.
**Observed [O]:**
VVV = 1 (the first drift sample is taken 1 s after the drift starts).
DDD = sample period (1800, 7200 or 14400 s; equal to the mission parameter DDT on float 11186).
All second differences 0 (p = 1).
NN equals the drift P/T/S sample count.
**Multi-part:** 0x79 has been observed in logs, so multi-part series do occur. Reassembly is the same as A.3.1.
**Decoder [D]:**
Accepts `(ID & 0xF8) == 0x78`.
Parts are kept with the drift composite.

`IsTimeDataComplete` requires contiguous indices and as many times as drift samples. Then the `D`/`d` lines switch to the time layout (A.3.3). Otherwise `# (Incomplete Drift Time Data)` is printed and the old layout is used.
`xmtps-list2json.py` uses these times instead of estimating drift times.

content.text: This part specifies the engineering message group of the ALAMO/ALTO X-message format: the SOLO-II-heritage engineering messages (0xE0, 0xE2, 0xE3), the built-in-test (BIT) messages (0xE5, 0xE6), the ALAMO dive-phase engineering messages (0xE7 descent, 0xE8 drift/park, 0xE9 ascent, 0xEA surface), the ice-detection engineering message (0xEC) and the system error codes that the 0xEA and 0xEC error lists carry. The valve message 0xEB is outside this part.

**Offsets.** Every offset in this part counts from the blob's ID byte (offset 0). Bytes 1–2 are the big-endian size `jj`, which counts the whole blob (ID, `jj`, data and the `;` terminator). Byte 3 of every message in this group is a format/version byte. The terminator `;` (0x3B) is the last byte, at offset `jj - 1`.

**Byte order.** All multi-byte fields are big-endian (most significant byte first). This holds for the IEEE-754 single-precision floats of BIT formats 9–11 too: the decoder assembles the four bytes big-endian into a `uint32` and bit-casts it to `float` (`f32` in `common/XDefinitions.h`).
**Types.** `u8`, `u16`, `u32` are unsigned integers; `i16` is a two's-complement signed integer; `f32` is an IEEE-754 binary32; `char[4]` is four ASCII bytes.
**Time epochs.** Two epochs are used, and each table names the one that applies:
A raw value of 0 decodes to "not a date/time" and is listed as `0000-00-00T00:00:00Z`.

**Sensor counts.** Fields marked *CTD counts* are raw 16-bit sensor codes converted with the float's profile gains and offsets from the Argo data message (0xF0): `value = counts / gain − offset`. The decoder uses the profile (not surface) gains for every engineering message. A result outside the valid range (pressure −5…2610 dbar, temperature −5…40 °C, salinity 2…41 PSU) or a zero gain gives the fill value −9.999.

**Fill values.** Fields that a message version does not carry keep the decoder's fill value: `0xFF` (`u8`), `0xFFFF` (`u16`), `0xFFFFFFFF` (`u32`), `−32768` (`i16`), or not-a-date/time. Some classes leave such fields uninitialized; this is noted per message. Fill values matter only to code that reads the decoded objects: the listings print only the fields each version carries.

**Version byte.** For 0xE7–0xEC, byte 3 is the "engineering version", written in hex (`0x10`, `0x11`, …). `XAlamoEngineering::engineering_version_as_float()` reads the high nibble as the major and the low nibble as the minor number (0x12 → 1.2). For 0xE5/0xE6, byte 3 is the "BIT format" (decimal 6–11). Firmware documents sometimes give the engineering version in decimal (`packetVersion = 17` = 0x11, `= 20` = 0x14).
**Common validation.** Every class below first calls `XMessage::CheckXMsgData()`, which:

items.text: rejects an empty blob, or one shorter than the class minimum (given per message);
checks the ID byte (skipped for 0xE5/0xE6, whose ID is checked later);
reads the size as `u16(d, 1) & 0x0FFF` (only the low 12 bits are used), rejects a size below 4 or larger than the received blob, and only warns when the blob is longer than the size;
rejects the blob unless byte `size − 1` is `;`.

content.text: The per-version size checks below compare the length of the received blob (`data.size()`), not the size field. A failed check throws `util::log::MessageException`; the message is then not assigned to the dive and the failure is logged.

**Listing output.** Engineering lines are written in the "Engineering Data" part of the dive listing, in this order of sections: Abort, BIT failed, BIT passed, Descent, Diagnostic Dive, Park/Drift, Ascent, Ice, Standard Dive, Surface. Each data line starts with a line-type tag, the serial number (`SN`), the dive number and a minor index (`midx`); the `#` lines above it are column headings and units.
The Python tool `bin/py/xmtps-list2json.py` maps these line types to the JSON engineering sections `bit`, `descent`, `drift`, `ascent`, `surface` and `ice` (see the README).

**Purpose.** These are the SOLO-II engineering messages, one per mission phase: 0xE0 after the first (diagnostic) dive of a mission, 0xE2 at the end of a normal dive cycle and 0xE3 after a mission abort. The SOLO-II X-format v2.0 document (20 Mar 2014) defines them as version 5. ALAMO floats do not send them: the v2.4 format overview marks all three "ALAMO supported: no, decoder supported: no".

**Decoder status.** `XEngDiagnostic` (0xE0), `XEngStandard` (0xE2) and `XEngAbort` (0xE3) are stubs. Each runs the common validation (expected ID, no minimum length beyond the size field) and decodes nothing; the listing gets the section heading ("Engineering (Diagnostic Dive)", "Engineering (Standard Dive)", "Engineering (Abort)") with an empty body. The 0xEA (versions 0x10–0x14) and 0xEC (version 0x11) error lists carry ALAMO firmware system error codes. A code is 16 bits on the wire (32 bits in 0xEA v0x10; the firmware enum `ASSERT_LOG_ERROR_*` is 32 bits wide). The **low byte** names the module or mission state and the **high byte** the specific error within it; a high byte of 0 is the generic error of that module. For example, 0x010C is module 0x0C (CTD), error 0x01 (pressure out of range), and 0x0114 is module 0x14 (ascend), error 0x01 (CTD).

The decoder does not translate codes: listings print them as `0x%08X` (e.g. `0x00000114`), and the Python tools pass the number through. The table merges `system-error-codes.txt` (names with the `ASSERT_LOG_ERROR_` prefix) and Appendix 2 of `nextgen_v10.5.0_blobs.txt` (`ERROR_` prefix).
No code is defined for module 0x09 or for 0x0315/0x0415 (park); a code not in the table should be reported as its module plus the raw high byte.
Between the decoder and the documents:

items.text: **0xEA v0x13/v0x14 bin counts.** The decoder reads offset 36 (v0x13) / 44 (v0x14) as the number of *empty bins* and 38 / 46 as the number of *raw samples*. The v2.4 spreadsheet, the 7.3.5 YAML, the 10.5.0 list and the 10.12.0 list all give the opposite order (samples, then empty bins). Listings checked so far (floats 9213, 9216, 9287, 11186) have 0 in both fields, so data cannot settle it yet; the documents suggest the decoder's `numEmptyBins` and `numRawSamples` columns are swapped. *(Fixed in build 3309: the decoder now reads samples before empty bins, as the documents give them.)*
**0xEC v0x11 bytes 20–21.** Decoder and 10.5.0 list: a 2-byte field (10.5.0: "seek time adjustment") before the error count at 22. Spreadsheet v2.4 and 7.3.5 YAML: error count at
The decoder matches transmitted messages; whether early-firmware 0x11 messages used the spreadsheet layout is unknown.

**Ice detection status values.** Spreadsheet: 0–3 (3 = temperature turnaround). 10.5.0: 0–5, with 2 = mixed layer, 3 = breakup, 4 = surface halt, 5 = complete, not found. Value 5 is seen in data. The firmware list is presumably current.
**0xEC threshold test temperature.** Spreadsheet: temperature counts (gain/offset). 7.3.5 and 10.5.0: °C × 1000. The decoder prints the raw number under a (degC) heading.

**BIT format 7/8 scales.** Air-pump maximum-load battery voltage: decoder ÷1000, spreadsheet and YAML ÷100. Oil-pump battery voltage: decoder and spreadsheet ÷1000, YAML ÷100. Oil pump test duration: spreadsheet gain 1000, decoder and YAML seconds.
**BIT format 8 signedness.** The pressure offset (and, per the YAML, both pressures) are signed; the decoder reads them unsigned.

**BIT format 8 in the spreadsheet.** The 0xE6 sheet gives a 16-bit CTD status and shifted offsets, and the 0xE5/0xE6 sheets swap the format 7/8 sizes (72/77); the 0xE5 size "77" conflicts with its own terminator at 75.

**BIT format 11 sizes.** The 10.12.0 list describes the format 11 layout (traveler errors, 20 thresholds, 264 bytes) but labels it `PacketVersion = 9`; a 10.12.0.1 float sends 11. The decoder also accepts a 256-byte format 11 that no document describes.

**BIT format 11 field names (10.12.0 list).** Offsets 141 and 175 are named "MaxAirPumpCurrent"/"MaxOilPumpCurrent" (duplicates) and 145/179 "Max…V12Current"; by comparison with 10.5.0 they are the 12 V current maximum and the battery voltage maximum, as the decoder reads them.
**BIT result bit 0x400** is set in real data and undocumented; bit 0x200 (accelerometer) is in 10.5.0 only.
**BIT format 9 "maximum air pressure"** is "inHg" in the 10.5.0 list; the decoder lists psi.

**E8/E9 version in 10.12.0.** The list gives `packetVersion = 17` (0x11) for 0xE8 and 0xE9 but the 0x12 layouts (22 and 19 bytes). If a float actually sent 0x11 with those sizes the decoder would reject it (it expects 28 and 13). A 10.12.0.1 float (11186) sends 0x12 for both, so the list is wrong on this point.
**Seek pump time adjustment type.** `I2` in 10.5.0 and 7.3.5, `U2` in 10.12.0; the decoder treats it as signed.
**0xE7 case vacuum scale.** 10.5.0 says ÷1000 for 0xE7 only (÷100 for 0xE8/0xE9 and in all other documents); the decoder uses ÷100.
**0xEA pressure offset reading** is `U2` in the 10.x lists, signed elsewhere; the decoder reads it signed.
**BIT format 9–11 "divisor" values** in the 10.5.0 list do not apply to the transmitted floats, which are already in engineering units.
**7.3.5 YAML** omits the version byte for 0xE7–0xEC (its field lists start at offset 4) and uses the surface gains for BIT pressures; the decoder uses the profile gains.
**Error-code tables.** `SURFACE_CTD_CRC` (0x2016) is only in the 10.5.0 appendix and `EXCEPTION` (0x00FF) only in `system-error-codes.txt`.
**Unexplained bytes.** 0xE7 v0x10 bytes 14–21 (23-byte form) / 20–25 (27-byte form), 0xEA v0x10 bytes 22–45 and 0xEA v0x12 bytes 12–13 are undocumented and not decoded.

content.text: The float sends its mission parameters: the dive-cycle, CTD, descent, park, ascent, surface, ice-detection, IMU and calibration settings stored in its non-volatile memory. ALAMO and ALTO floats send them in a binary format at each surfacing when `APT` = 1, as two blobs, D0 and D1. SOLO-II floats send an ASCII dump of their EEPROM instead, only in answer to a ground-station `P` command. The low nibble of the ID is the part index (`D0` = part 0, `D1` = part 1, and so on).

rows: `NAMExx=vvvvv|` records, 6-character name, `=`, 5-character value and `|`, with no gaps between records. Example: `PchSec=   -1|MaxHrs= 1440|dBarGo=   -1|...| XP2=    0| XPdly=    0|`.

content.text: SOLO2 says the dump takes 4 SBD messages: D0, D1 and D2 of 328 bytes each, and D3 of 7 bytes. It also says each parameter takes 15 bytes, but the record template it gives has 13 characters (see C.5).

The two encodings are told apart by byte 3. XF2.4 calls it "message encoding format type identifier": 0 = binary (ALAMO), 1-255 = ASCII (SOLO-II). In an ASCII dump, byte 3 is the first character of the first parameter name, so it is never 0. NG10.12 calls the same byte `MissionConfigVersion` and gives it the value 0.

The active decoder, `XMfaMissionCfg`, never reads byte 3. A SOLO-II ASCII D0 would go through the binary path and fail as an unsupported firmware version, because bytes 4-7 would be ASCII characters.

items.text: From 4.5.63 on, the parameter list is longer than one SBD-sized blob and is cut in two. D0 holds the header and the first parameters, and D1 holds the rest from offset 3. Firmware before 4.5.63 sends D0 only, except 4.6.61: its D0 ends at `SAN` like 4.5.63, but the decoder doesn't decode a D1 for it.
Where the cut falls depends on the firmware:

5.0.61 to 10.6.x (D0 = 328 bytes): D0 ends with `PFV1` (offsets 325-326). D1 starts with `PFV2`. NG10.5 numbers the parameters as one contiguous blob; D1 offset = NG10.5 offset - 324 (for example `PFV2`: 327 → 3, `PPE`: 415 → 91).
6.5.77 and 6.8.5: D0 ends with `PFV0`, and D1 starts with `PFV1`.

5.0.61.1, and 10.7 and later (D0 = 327 bytes): D0 ends with `PSM` (offset 325). D1 starts with `PSD`. In 10.7 the `PNB`/`PNC`/`PXC` BIT thresholds (6 bytes) were dropped, so `PFV2`, `PDT` and `PSM` (5 bytes) now fit in D0.

Assembly [decoder] (`AssignMessage`): the part index is `ID & 0x0F`. Only indexes 0 and 1 are accepted (`XMSG_MAX_MFA_MISS` = 2), so D2-D7 are rejected with "Message index exceeds". Each part is stored per dive, and a repeated part replaces the earlier one.
On D0: the firmware word is read from bytes 4-7 (the blob must be at least 8 bytes), D0 is decoded, and a stored D1 is decoded again.
On D1: it is decoded only if D0 is already stored. Otherwise it is kept until D0 arrives.
[decoder] The decoder never looks at the D0 parameters version (offset 8) to choose a layout. Only the firmware word does.

content.text: The "Mission Configuration" section is printed once per dive, from the dive's D0 and D1. Three styles exist.

items.text: **`mis` groups**, for layouts `02006200` and `02006900` (firmware 2.0.62 to 4.1.61). A header line `mis SN dive idx 0xFWWORD` is followed by groups of fixed-width columns, one line per group with a minor index `midx`, each group with its own column-name and unit comment lines. Example group: `mis SN dive idx midx MSN DTD MDS APT XAS`.

**`MIS` header and `mis` groups**, for 4.2.62, 4.3.61, 4.4.61 and 4.6.61 (listing `04026200`). The header is `MIS SN dive idx 0xVV 0xFWWORD sensor-type # name`, followed by `mis` groups as in style 1.
**`MIS` header and `m` lines**, for 4.5.63 and every firmware from 5.0.61 on. Format:

#      SN dive        CfgMsgVer       FWVer sensor-type        sensor-type-name
MIS  9213    1             0x18  0x0A0C0032           0      # RBR
# --- General --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#      SN dive idx param      value      units          desc
m    9213    1   0 MSN            1      [-]          # dive cycle number
m    9213    1   3 MDS         1000      [dBar]       # maximum depth
m    9213    1  42 CPP1           1.000  [sec]        # interval 1 sample period
m    9213    1 133 ICT           -1.40   [degC]       # threshold temperature
`MIS` is `MIS %5d %4d 0x%02X 0x%08X %11d # name`: serial number, dive, parameters version (offset 8), firmware word, CTD type and its name (`RBR`, `SBE` or `unknown`).

Each `m` line is `m SN dive idx NAME value [units] # description`. `idx` counts the `m` lines from 0, in listing order, not in message order. Integers are printed with `%10d`. Scaled values use 1-4 decimals.

Sections, in order: General; BIT (layouts before 10.7 only); Calibration Coefficients; Start-of-Mission Trigger; Diagnostic Dive; Mission Phase; Profile; Profile - Dynamic Salinity Correction (only in the `0A050000`, `0A060231` and `0A080031` listings); Profile - Binning Configuration (CPN/CPP depend on the CTD type: RBR scaled, SBE raw dBar, unknown raw); Profile - Raw Sampling; Profile - Surface Offset Correction; Pump Characteristics; Descent (General, Fall Time-Series, Stages 1-3); Drift/Park (General, Seek, Start of Profile Trigger, Fall to Profile Pressure); Ascent/Profile (General, Rise Time-Series, Ice-Detection, Ice-Detection Summer and Winter); Surface (General, Air Pump, Sampling, Sat./Comm., Abort/Beacon Mode); Surface - Wave-Field Measurement (`WST`, only in the WIMS listings `08000000`, `0A060231` and `0A080031`; the `06057700` listing prints `WMT` instead, which that layout never decodes, so it always shows 65535).
A 10.12.0.x listing has 177 `m` lines.
The Python tools keep each `m` line (section, index, name, value, units) in the dive JSON as `mission.entries`, and keep `cfgver`, `fwver` and `ctdtype` from the `MIS` line.
If no D0 has arrived, the firmware word is still 0xFFFFFFFF and the section is the single line `# Incomplete mission parameters.`

content.text: XF2.4 defines only the ID, size and terminator.

Production [inferred, from all 2026 echoes on argus]. The echo is the uploaded command text exactly as sent: the commands separated by `;`, ending with `MIC 1` (which the upload itself ends with). Besides the text, the blob carries 8-9 bytes of undocumented binary data. Its position varies:

items.text: **After the text:** seen in most echoes. The bytes are NULs, but the last one is sometimes not (0x01, 0x08 and 0x80 have been seen).
**Before the text:** all NULs. Seen in the dive 0 echoes of the Lowell ALAMOs (10.12.1) and of 11190 (10.12.0.1).

content.text: The commands use the mission-parameter mnemonics, with a phase index where the parameter has one (`dft 0 100` sets `DFT0` to 100). They are echoed in whatever case they were uploaded in. A long upload may come back as two consecutive echo blobs in the same session. When several uploads are queued, each one is echoed separately. Because `;` also appears inside the text, the end of the blob must be found from `jj`, not by looking for the first `;`.
**Verification against uploads (2026-10-25).** The uploads sent with `upload-alamo-cmd` since 2026-01-01 (`/data1/alamo/data/sbd/outgoing`) were compared with the echoes in the RAW files:

items.text: 261 uploads were echoed back exactly, some in two pieces.
23 were not echoed, all to floats that have not called in since.
A few were not echoed although the float called in. One, to 9213 on 2026-09-28, verifiably did not take effect: its mission parameters still show the old values.
A handful of echoes match no recorded upload (`ppe`, `wst` commands). They were presumably sent another way.
`XMissionCmdEcho` calls `CheckXMsgData(data, 0xDE, -1)`. That checks the ID, that `jj` (lower 12 bits) is at least 4 and no more than the data received, and that the terminator is at `jj - 1`.

The float reduces the data on board to one-sided acceleration auto- and cross-spectra and sends one spectral component per blob. Shore-side processing gives wave height and direction. The format of the raw IMU time series was defined in XF2.4 but is not decoded. The decoder treats 0xC1 and 0xC3 the same way: the blob's version and type fields decide how it is decoded, not the ID.

One dive sends six blobs, one per component, often one per SBD packet. Floats whose segment is too long for one blob split a component over several blobs using the first-bin index.

items.text: An invalid full-scale-range byte logs an error and falls back to ASSF = 2048 (the 4 g entry).
Effective spectral scale (WIMS user manual rev. 3.15, "Scale Sensitivity"): ESSF = 32768 · ASSF · G² · U · f_e² / (2 N²), in counts per g²/Hz, where:
G = Q / 8 is the acceleration gain (Q the raw Q3 gain; G = 1 when Q is 0, and for v0/v1);
U = 1 - (5L/4 + 1) / N is the mean square of the firmware's Tukey window, with taper length L = round((N - 1) · 64 / 256) (`wav.twalp` = 64, which the header does not carry; U = 0.68359 for N = 256);
f_e = f_base / (d + 1) is the true effective sample rate, not the doubled rate of C.3.8.

Example: v2 at ±4 g, G = 4, N = 256, f_e = 2.5 Hz gives ESSF = 35000; at f_e = 5 Hz, 140000. Before 2026-10-28 (build 3332) the decoder used ESSF = ⌊ASSF · Q² / 64⌋ = ASSF · G², the formula of manual revisions up to 3.14, which ignores f_e, N and the window (32768 in the example).
Acceleration spectrum: S_aa [g²/Hz] = counts / ESSF.

Displacement spectrum [decoder]: S_ηη [m²/Hz] = g² · S_aa / (2πf)⁴, with g = 9.80665 m/s² and π = 3.14159265359. It is clamped to at most +999.9999. The cross terms `Cxy`, `Qzx` and `Qzy` are also clamped to at least -999.9999.
[decoder] ASSF, gain, f_base, d and N are kept per dive and overwritten by each blob, so the last blob decoded sets the scale for all components.

content.text: For bin k (0 … N/2 - 1), f_k = f_s · k / N, with f_s = f_base / (d + 1). Bin 0 is the DC bin; the last bin is f_s/2 - f_s/N. WIMS firmware up to 2.01.00614b labels its own output one bin high, (k + 1) · f_s / N, and the decoder did the same until 2026-10-26 (see below).

items.text: Build 3238 (2025-10) went back to `fs·(i+1)/seglen`.

2026-10-26: `fs·(k0+i)/seglen`, with bin 0 the DC bin. The WIMS firmware copies FFT bins 0 to N/2 - 1, so `fs·(i+1)/seglen` was one bin too high; an intercomparison with NDBC buoy 41047 confirmed the offset.
The 2026-10-24 fix added k0 to k, so bins in a blob with k0 > 0 get the right frequency. Before that, the frequency ignored k0.
[decoder] The spectral array holds N/2 bins per dive. A bin that no blob filled keeps frequency -99 and fill values. For example 9287 and 9291 send only bins 0-50 of N/2 = 256.

Newer sensor firmware truncates the spectrum to a range of frequencies, so a blob may carry fewer than N/2 bins (n from `jj`, as in C.3.3 and C.3.4). [decoder] Only the n bins in the blob are decoded; before build 3315 the decoder tried all N/2 and logged "wave sample index exceeds message size" for every truncated blob.
[decoder] Bins that would reach past N/2 (k0 + i ≥ N/2) are not decoded, and a warning is logged; before build 3315 `vector::at` threw and the whole blob was discarded.

content.text: [inferred from production; README 0.6.3235] Firmware 0x0A060231, 0x0A080031, 0x0A090131 and 0x0A0A0031 send only every other spectral value: the first half of the N/2 bins holds the spectrum at twice the bin spacing, and the second half is zeros. [decoder] `XFloatDiveData::ResolveWaveBinSpacing()` runs after each 0xC1/0xC3 blob and after each mission configuration message, so the result does not depend on message order. It takes the firmware word from the dive's own D0 or, without one, the float's latest; if that word is one of these, `XWave::set_every_other_bin(true)`:

items.text: sets f_s' = 2 · f_base / (d + 1), which also becomes the `WVS` `fsam`; the ESSF (C.3.6) still uses the true f_e;

sets the frequency of every received bin, i = 0 … N/2 - 1, to f_i = f_s' · i / N (f_s' · (i + 1) / N before 2026-10-26); bins not received keep -99. [inferred from the NDBC 41047 intercomparison, whose offset matches one decoded bin] The floats send the even WIMS bins (0, 2, 4, …), so bin i holds WIMS FFT bin 2i.

content.text: When the firmware word is unknown (it is not kept across decoder restarts), `XWave::LooksLikeEveryOtherBin()` decides from the data: every bin of the upper half was received and is zero in all six components, and some bin of the lower half has a nonzero Szz. Truncated spectra leave the upper bins unreceived, not zero, so they do not match. Before 2026-10-28 (build 3332) the correction was keyed only on the float's latest known firmware word, so blobs decoded before any D0 had been received were not corrected.

The spectral values are left as they are, so the zero second half is still listed, at frequencies above f_s/2. 10.12.1.31 (0x0A0C0131) and 10.7.1.31 (0x0A070131) are WIMS firmware too, but they are not in the correction list (C.5).

content.text: This layout has no version byte. Byte 3 is the packet index and byte 5 the ASSF index. The current decoder would therefore read a raw packet as a spectral version (packet index 0 or 1) or ignore it. In the v2 layout, byte 5 is the mode, and mode 0 (raw) is accepted but nothing is decoded. The old raw decoder and its `WAV`/`wav` listing lines are commented out in `XWave.cpp`.

items.text: `CheckXMsgData(data, -1, 17)`: the blob is at least 17 bytes, `jj` (lower 12 bits) is at least 4 and no more than the data received, and the byte at `jj - 1` is 0x3B. Extra bytes after `jj` only give a warning.
Version 0, 1 or 2; any other version is ignored without an error.
v2: mode 0 or 1 (otherwise it throws), and `jj` at least 19.

Each bin is read only while its two bytes lie before the terminator. For v1 the loop stops when 2i + 17 ≥ `jj`; for v2, when 2i + 20 ≥ `jj`. At most N/2 bins are read. The 2026-10-24 fix corrected the v2 bound, which used to read one bin past the terminator and broke the 51-bin floats' products.
Unsupported axis/type combinations throw, and the blob is dropped (`CATCH_BLOCK`).

content.text: The section "Ocean Surface Wave-Field Data" is printed when the dive has wave data with N > 0. Only versions 1 and 2 print anything: a dive whose wave blobs are all version 0 gets an empty section. In the example, the `wvs` and `wvm` values were listed before build 3332 with ESSF 32768; the current decoder lists them about 7% lower (ESSF 35100).

items.text: `WVS` (`WVS %5d %4d 0x%02X %4d %8.4f %4d %5d %8d %6.3f %10.1f`; `essf` was `%8d` before build 3332) has these columns:
`vers`: the version;
`slen`: N;
`fsam`: f_s, doubled by the C.3.8 correction;
`fbase`: f_base;
`fdiv`: d + 1, not the raw divider;
`assf`;
`again`: G;
`essf`.

`wvs` (`%8.4f` frequency, `%+11.5f` values) gives one line per bin, idx = 0 … N/2 - 1, with the acceleration spectra in g²/Hz. The columns are always in the order **zz, yy, xx, xy, zx, zy**: Szz, Syy, Sxx, Cxy, Qzx, Qzy.

`wvm` (`%+11.4f`) gives the same bins as displacement spectra in m²/Hz. It **must use the same column order as `wvs`** (zz, yy, xx, xy, zx, zy) under the same header. Builds 3234-3289 (2025-09 to 2026-10-24) printed `wvm` as xx, xy, yy, zz, zx, zy under the zz-first header, so `wvm` columns in listings from those builds are mislabeled. The 2026-10-24 fix restored the `wvs` order. Nothing downstream parses `wvm`.
Fill: a component never received is -999.99999 in `wvs`. In `wvm` the same fill prints as `-1000.0000`, because `%+11.4f` rounds -999.99999. Unfilled bins have frequency -99.0000.

content.text: MIZ floats (for example 9213 and 9216 with firmware 10.12.0.32) listen for acoustic navigation and communication signals (CACST, "communication and navigation" pings) in scheduled listening windows. Each listening window and each received signal is reported in its own 0xCA blob, with a subtype byte at offset 3. Shore-side processing uses the times of arrival to position the float under ice. The type ID was 0xC0 in decoder builds before 3249 (2026-05/06); the decoder now uses 0xCA (`XMSG_TYPE_ID_MIZ_ACOUSTIC`). XF2.4 lists 0xC0 "acoustic position" as unsupported, with an empty sheet. DF7.3.5's blob 192 (0xC0) is a different text payload (`sensor_type`, `payload_index`, 333-character text).

content.text: Mission configuration:

items.text: **Parameters version.** NG10.5 and NG10.12 document `MissionParamsVersion` = 23 (0x17). Production 10.12.0.x floats send 0x18. The decoder doesn't use the field.

**Byte 3 of D0.** XF2.4 calls it the encoding type (0 = binary, otherwise ASCII). NG10.5 calls it "Message version" and NG10.12 `MissionConfigVersion` = 0. The active decoder ignores it, so a SOLO-II ASCII dump would be misread (C.1.2).

**Byte 7 of the firmware word.** The task calls it "build". NG10.5 calls it "Float model" and NG10.12 "Product". Values such as 0x31 (WIMS) and 0x32/0x33 (MM2/Micro-ALTO) suggest a product or variant code. The decoder uses all 32 bits as the key.
**`DRT` type.** NG10.5 and NG10.12 give I2; the decoder reads U2. **`MSN`**: NG10.5 says I2, NG10.12 U2.
**XF2.4 against the decoder for old firmware:**
2.0.69 (XF2.4: 323 bytes with `CTF`/`CTL`/`CTU` but no ice block; decoder: 322 bytes with ice, the same as XF2.4's 2.5.62 layout).
3.0.65 (XF2.4: 331 bytes ending `SPT`, `SSP`; decoder: 328 bytes, no `SPT`/`SSP`).
4.2.62 (XF2.4: 327 bytes with no gap at 119 and a 5-byte "empty?" field at 161; decoder: 323 bytes, `IST` at 120, `DNS` at 162).
4.6.61 (XF2.4: one 336-byte D0 ending `SSP`; decoder: 328 bytes ending `SAN`, and D1 not decoded).
The decoder's sizes presumably come from real messages; the spreadsheet looks like intent.
**`ICF`/`ICW` as U1** in the 2.0.69 to 4.1.61 decoders: only the most significant byte of each 4-byte mask is decoded.
**10.7.1.1 D1** is 88 bytes and probably carries `PPC`/`PPE`, but the decoder doesn't decode them.
**0x08020000 and 0x0A020201** decode but have no listing function, so they get the generic "unsupported" listing.
**Listing bugs:**
`DRT` prints `DRA`. *(Fixed in build 3309.)*
The `PPC0`/`PPC1` values are swapped against their labels. *(Fixed in build 3309.)*
`PPC`/`PPE` are not listed for 10.7-10.14 non-WIMS floats.
The 6.5.77 listing shows `WMT` = 65535 because that layout doesn't decode it.
**Units:**
`AHR` (NG10.5: cm/s; listed value/1000 m/s, so 1000 lists as 1.000 m/s).
`ASI` (NG10.5: s; listed value/1000 s).
`IST` (header comment: 1/10 PSU; listed value/100).
`SAN`/`SAX` (NG10.5: psi; listed value/1000).
`DRA` labeled m/s, printed raw.
`XAS` and `CST` codes differ between NG10.5 and XF2.4.
These need confirming with MRV.
**SOLO-II ASCII record length.** SOLO2 says 15 bytes per parameter, but its template `NAMExx=vvvvv|` is 13 characters. And 324 bytes of text per 328-byte blob is not a whole number of either.
**D2-D7.** SOLO-II used D0-D3 for the ASCII dump. The binary decoder rejects anything above D1.

content.text: No format document describes ID 0xFF; the decoder's ID list calls it `UNKNOWN`. Everything below is **[inferred]** from the 6,262 0xFF blobs in the production RAW files (survey of 2026-10-27, 160 floats, all firmware from 10.2 to 10.14, WIMS and not). Before build 3321 the decoder logged each one as `Unknown X message ID: 0xff` and dropped it (several hundred warnings a day).

**Layout.** The usual ID and 12-bit size (bytes 0-2, A.1.3) and `;` terminator, with a record type at byte 3 and, except for 0xDB, its version at byte 4. Several record types are also X-message IDs (0xCA, 0xD1, 0xDB, 0xEC), but the records do not match those messages: the type is a separate code space.

rows: u16 counter @5, u32 time @7, u16 count @11, u32 time @13, u32 value @17 (0 in nearly all)
u16 0 @5, u16 float serial number @7, then 3 (v0x10: 2) configuration bytes
text: a processor fault dump, or all NUL
CTD exchange: u16 command length @4, command, u16 reply length, reply

items.text: **Times** are UNIX seconds (e.g. 0x62BF7945 = 2022-07-01T22:46:29Z, 23 minutes before that packet's Iridium session), or seconds since the controller started when they are below 2000-01-01 (37% of the 0xCA times, e.g. 402). The decoder lists the latter as `+402s`.

**0xCA** records come in pairs with a 0xD1 record 8-17 s earlier, several pairs per startup packet. The value is a few tenths of a unit around zero (-0.32 to +0.10 in the examples), most likely the surface pressure in dBar measured at the event; code 0x004002 is the most common event. The 0xD1 counter increases by one per pair across a float's life (4 on 9166 in 2022; 71-73 on 9304 in 2026), so it is probably a controller start (reset) count, with the start time and, in the second time field, an uptime in seconds (`+207s`). What `count` counts is unknown.

**0xAE** carries the float's serial number (0x23FB = 9211, 0x245B = 9307, 0x2D6D = 11629) and 2-3 small configuration values, sent during the startup tests. They may be the pump and battery types that the BIT format 11 "traveler" errors (B.2.6, MissingPumpType, MissingBatteryType) refer to.

**0xFA** is an ARM Cortex-M fault report: `r7`, `sp`, `excrt` (EXC_RETURN), `psr`, the fault status registers `hfsr`, `cfsr`, `mmfar`, `bfar`, `shcsr`, and the stacked `s.r0`-`s.r3`, `s.r12`, `s.lr`, `s.pc`, `s.psr`, one per line (CR LF), in hex. It records a controller crash, for example 9304 dive 0 (firmware 10.12.1.31) with `cfsr 00000082` (a data access violation at a precise address). Empty reports are all NUL.

**0xDB** records the RBR CTD exchanges of 9280 (10.6.2.1) and three other floats (11148, 11151, 11330): the command text, e.g. `ctdrw fetch\r|5` (a literal backslash-r; the `|` digit is perhaps a timeout), and the CTD's reply, e.g. `2024-03-15 22:57:12.000, 25.1567, 10.1491, 117.6462, 25.6469\r\n` or a calibration (`calibration 3 label = pressure_00, ...`) or `id model = RBRargo3, ...` line. The lengths account for every byte of the blob.
